page.layout: One block of running text in a single column, with no margin notes. Reference numbers stand inline in the text. Below the last line: catchword at the right and gathering signature at the left.

main_text.p: Juravit Jacob per Timore patris sui Isaac. Isa.8.13. Jehovam exercituum sanctifica-bitis: & ipse sit timor vester, & pavor vester. In his & similibus dictis, Jehovah ipse, μετωνυμίας, Timor dicitur. Ac pij eo nomine Timentes dicutur. Psal.15.4. Vilis est in oculis eius homo nihili, sed timē tes Jehovam honorat.
1. Joan.4.18. Timor non est in charita-te: expleta charitas foras eijcit timorem seu metum: quoniam timor cruciatū habet. qui autem timet, non est perfectus in charitate.

Discimus, aliud esse timorem Jehovae, qui cum fiducia misericordiae, charitate & gaudio (ob conscientiae pacem) coniungitur, & filialis, propter adoptionis Spiritum, recte dicitur: aliud metum seu timorem servilem, qui charitatis expers, κόλασιν habet. In hoc tamen dicto speciem χαρίσματος Spiritus sancti significat.

Interesse autem inter Timorem seu reverentiam & Metum, etiam Spartiata ille monuit, qui cum interrogatus esset, Cur Lacones promte in acie periclitarentur, respondit: ὅτι ἀνδρείαν[?] τὰς[?] ἡγεμόνας ἐμα-χόμεθα[?], φοβεῖσθαι. Saepe tamen promiscuè in Scripturis illa verba [?]ἀνδρεῖσθαι καὶ φοβεῖσθαι

page.notes: Long s rendered as s throughout (printed f). The Greek words marked [?] are not clearly legible on the scan, and the Greek of the Spartan reply and the final phrase should be checked against a clearer image. "timē tes": the mark over the e is ambiguous (possibly a line-end abbreviation); "dicutur" may carry a tilde. Printed "Iurauit", "Iacob", "Iehouam", "Ioan" and "Iehouah" have their i/j and u/v letters normalised per the rules. The Bayerische Staatsbibliothek stamp is omitted.
